nodes.summary: Kourovka Problem 11.93: do block lattices generate all lattices? The proposition, asked by D. M. Smirnov, that the block lattices of finite groups generate the variety of all lattices. Here the blocks of a group $G$ are the cosets of normal subgroups of $G$ and the empty set; ordered by inclusion they form the block lattice of $G$, whose meet is intersection and whose join of two blocks is the intersection of all…
nodes.title: Kourovka Problem 11.93: do block lattices generate all lattices?

nodes.summary: For subsets $X$ and $Y$ of a group $G$, their block join is the intersection of all blocks of $G$ that contain $X \cup Y$. Since blocks are closed under intersections and $G$ itself is a block, this is the smallest block containing $X \cup Y$; for blocks $X$ and $Y$ it is their join in the block lattice of $G$.
nodes.title: Join in the block lattice

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a group and $v$ an assignment of a subset $v(n)$ of $G$ to each variable $x_n$. The value of a lattice term under $v$ is defined by recursion on the term: the variable $x_n$ has value $v(n)$, a meet $s \wedge t$ has as value the intersection of the values of $s$ and $t$, and a join $s \vee t$ has as value the block join of the values of $s$ and $t$, the intersection of all blocks of $G$ containing their…
nodes.title: Evaluation of lattice terms in the block lattice

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a lattice and $v$ an assignment of an element $v(n)$ of $L$ to each variable $x_n$. The value of a lattice term under $v$ is defined by recursion on the term: the variable $x_n$ has value $v(n)$, and a join $s \vee t$ or meet $s \wedge t$ has as value the join or meet in $L$ of the values of $s$ and $t$.
nodes.title: Evaluation of lattice terms

nodes.summary: A subset $X$ of a group $G$ is a block if it is empty or a coset $gN$ of a normal subgroup $N$ of $G$ (Kourovka Notebook, Archive 9.62). Ordered by inclusion, the blocks of $G$ form the block lattice $C(G)$.
nodes.title: Blocks of a group

nodes.summary: Lattice terms in the variables $x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots$ are built inductively: each variable $x_n$ is a term, and for terms $s$ and $t$ their join $s \vee t$ and their meet $s \wedge t$ are terms.
